# Scalar native stages

Submit main.py AND engine.cpp under submission/. The JSON compiler contract
is PROTOCOL.md; the same submission also provides the three native stages
below. They exercise the interval compiler, image builder and actual packed
lookup kernel independently. Native stages do not optimize a plan.

The build interface is exactly:

    g++ -O2 -std=c++17 /workspace/submission/engine.cpp -o /workspace/tmp/engine

engine.cpp is one translation unit and may include supporting .hpp/.cpp files
from the submission tree. The offline GCC toolchain supports unsigned
__int128. Require no ISA extension beyond baseline x86-64. The provided
engine.hpp retains scalar interval/tree code with legacy 64-bit and fixed-depth
limitations; packed integration and lookup are unfinished. Extend it to meet
these interfaces. Function/class names and implementation strategy are free.

A native invocation reads one whitespace-delimited ASCII request through EOF,
writes the specified token sequence to stdout and exits zero. Whitespace
between tokens is arbitrary. Decimal output integers use ordinary canonical
notation; keys are lowercase 32-digit unsigned hexadecimal. Hop -1 means null;
hop 0 is a real next hop. No diagnostics belong on stdout.

Native requests are structurally valid inputs satisfying the conditions below.
Malformed/out-of-domain native input has no required response. The JSON entry
still must handle every invalid request as specified in PROTOCOL.md. Each
native operation, including needed compilation, has the same 120-second wall,
process/memory/file/output and scratch restrictions as a whole JSON request.
Native input is at most 16 MiB; stdout 64 MiB and stderr 1 MiB. Public limits
are not reset per route, node or address. Compiler products stay in scratch.

## ATLAS

Input tokens:

    ATLAS n
    start length hop                 (n rows)

n is 0..30000. Each start is a 32-digit key, length is 0..128, and hop is
0..2147483647. Starts have already had host bits masked. The normalized
(start,length) routes are unique and may arrive in any order. This is one
RIB version; there are no transaction commands in this stage.

Output tokens:

    R
    start hop                        (R rows)

Return the unique maximal forwarding runs defined by PROTOCOL.md, starting at
zero and coalescing adjacent equal next hops. Null is -1. The empty RIB has
one full-domain null run. This standalone stage may return more than 64 runs
(at most 2*n+1); the JSON compiler enforces its own per-version/whole-request
run limits after compilation. No artificial upper-domain endpoint is emitted.

## PACK

Input tokens:

    PACK R N A
    start hop                        (R rows)
    lo span mode cached b child_id... (N rows)
    address                          (A rows)

1<=R<=64, 1<=N<=2*R-1 and 0<=A<=8192. Starts/hops describe valid canonical
runs, with -1 for null and other hops 0..2147483647. Node IDs are row indices
0..N-1 in breadth-first order; ID0 is the root. A row has exactly b child IDs.
b=0 denotes a leaf; otherwise b is 2..9. All node ranges, partitions, modes,
residency flags and ordering obey the legal-tree rules in PROTOCOL.md. There
is no optimization requirement or cache budget for this standalone stage;
its supplied cached bits are serialized as given. Addresses are 32-digit keys.

Output tokens:

    image
    hop run path_length node_offset... (A rows)

Build the unique exact FIDX version2 byte image for THAT supplied layout,
including all required minimal allocation/zero padding. image is lowercase
hexadecimal. Report each actual packed lookup's hop, zero-based run index and
root-to-leaf byte-offset path. Layout choices are inputs, not selected here.

## TRACE

Input tokens:

    TRACE A
    image
    address                          (A rows)

0<=A<=8192. image is ANY valid FIDX version2 image for 1..64 canonical runs,
including arbitrary legal topology, modes, cached flags and next hops. Its
bytes are the complete source of keys/children/hops; no RIB, starts array,
layout objects or process state is supplied. Apply predecessor/equality rules
from PROTOCOL.md. Return A rows of hop, run, path_length and node_offset tokens
in input address order, in the same form as PACK's answer rows. With A=0 the
correct native output has no tokens. Different invocations share no state.

The public command remains:

    python3 check.py submission/main.py

It runs the JSON candidate in bounded real children, then compiles engine.cpp
as another bounded child and runs the small .native fixtures. It uses only
public files. Empty/nonJSON/nonzero JSON responses fail; incorrect/extra native
tokens or a failed native build/run fail. These fixtures are sanity checks;
all published stage and JSON semantics remain mandatory at full bounds.
=== instruction ===
Build the cache-budgeted IPv6 image compiler in `/workspace`.
Read `PROTOCOL.md` and `NATIVE.md` for the complete JSON and native contracts.
Extend the supplied scalar C++ library and Python driver; compilation is unfinished.
Apply ordered route transactions and retain every immutable FIB version.
Support all IPv6 prefix lengths `/0` through `/128` with exact unsigned arithmetic.
Compile each version into maximal forwarding intervals and a packed search image.
Choose tree partitions, node encodings, and cached nodes jointly across versions.
Honor the shared cache-page budget and globally minimize the specified cost pair.
The burst-aware cost is a published software model, not measured hardware time.
Return images, forwarding changes, and lookup paths in one JSON result on stdout.
Provide native ATLAS, PACK and TRACE stages that compile and search actual image bytes.
Any valid globally optimal layout is accepted; there is no preferred tree shape.
Reject an invalid whole request exactly as specified; emit no partial answer.
Submit `submission/main.py`, `submission/engine.cpp`, and supporting sources.
The entry is `python3 -B /workspace/submission/main.py`, reading stdin through EOF.
Use Python 3.11 standard library and the provided offline C++17 toolchain.
Run `python3 check.py submission/main.py` as the provided nonroot user.
The public checker uses real bounded children and accepts equivalent optimal images.
Satisfy the whole maximum batch; no external service or special hardware is needed.
